title: India Drawn Against Pakistan in SAFF Championship 2026 Group Stage
excerpt: The defending champions will face Pakistan on November 5 in Dhaka, adding a high-stakes political dimension to South Asian football's premier tournament.
body:
• India has been drawn in Group B alongside Pakistan and Maldives for the SAFF Championship 2026 in Dhaka
  • The India-Pakistan match is scheduled for November 5, marking a rare competitive football meeting between the rivals
  • Bangladesh will host the tournament as Group A top seeds, alongside Bhutan and Sri Lanka
  • India are the defending champions, having won the title at the last edition

The draw for the SAFF Championship 2026 has placed India and Pakistan in the same group, setting up one of South Asian football's most anticipated encounters. The tournament, scheduled for November in Dhaka, will see defending champions India face Pakistan on November 5 in a match that transcends sport.

Group Dynamics

Group B pairs India with Pakistan and Maldives, while Group A features hosts Bangladesh alongside Bhutan and Sri Lanka. India enter as clear favourites in their group, sitting comfortably above both opponents in the FIFA rankings, but the India-Pakistan dynamic ensures the match will carry a weight that form guides cannot capture.

https://x.com/MarcusMergulhao/status/2083523718949785688

Football meetings between India and Pakistan are rare compared to their cricket rivalry, making each encounter an event in its own right. The last competitive meeting saw India dominate, but Pakistan's football programme has been investing in youth development and coaching infrastructure, narrowing the gap incrementally.

Maldives, the third team in Group B, have historically been competitive in SAFF tournaments and cannot be overlooked. Their compact, well-organised defensive style has troubled Indian sides in past editions.

India's Title Defence

India will enter Dhaka as defending champions, having won the previous edition under coach Igor Stimac's successor. The Indian squad has undergone generational change in recent years, with younger players from the Indian Super League forming the core of the national team.

The ISL's professionalisation of Indian club football has lifted the overall standard of the national team, but SAFF tournaments have occasionally produced upsets. India's dominance of the competition — they have won the title a record number of times — is not guaranteed in a knockout format where one poor game can end a campaign.

"Every time India plays Pakistan, the scoreboard tells one story and the atmosphere tells another. These matches mean everything to both sets of fans."

— All India Football Federation statement

The Dhaka Factor

Hosting the tournament in Bangladesh adds another layer of complexity. Bangladeshi fans are passionate about football, and the Dhaka crowd will create a hostile environment for visiting teams. India have historically performed well in Bangladesh, but the atmosphere can be intense.

For the Indian diaspora globally, the November 5 India-Pakistan clash will be appointment viewing. While cricket remains the primary sporting rivalry between the two nations, football encounters carry a raw intensity partly because they are so infrequent. Social media engagement around previous SAFF India-Pakistan matches has rivalled that of all but the biggest cricket fixtures.

What's Next

Both teams will play regional friendlies and FIFA window matches in the lead-up to November. India's squad selection will be closely watched, with several ISL stars pushing for places. Pakistan, meanwhile, will look to their diaspora-based players and domestic league performers to mount a credible challenge in what will be their biggest football match of the year.
